title: Every pooling rule has its world: matching probability combination rules to situations and stakes
abstract: arXiv:2608.11275v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Systems often need to combine two numerical assessments of the same yes/no question. The appropriate formula depends on what the numbers represent and on how the sources are related. Averaging is correct when one of several alternative interpretations applies; multiplying odds is correct when probability reports are based on conditionally independent evidence and a common prior; and probabilities of alternative successful derivations require their dependence or shared evidence to be taken into account.   We state the assumptions behind several common combination rules and derive the corresponding combined probabilities. Two groups of Monte Carlo experiments address different questions. First, controlled generating mechanisms verify that the derived rule recovers the correct probability in the situations for which its assumptions hold. Second, the same mechanisms measure the consequences of using a mismatched rule, using logarithmic sco

translated_title: 每个合并规则都有其适用场景：将概率合并规则与情境和风险相匹配
translated_abstract: 系统经常需要合并两个关于同一是非问题的数值评估。合适的公式取决于这些数字所代表的意义以及来源之间的关联方式。当多种替代解释之一适用时，取平均值是正确的；当概率报告基于条件独立证据和共同先验时，乘以几率是正确的；而替代成功推导的概率则需要考虑其依赖性或共享证据。我们阐述了几个常见合并规则背后的假设，并推导出相应的合并概率。两组蒙特卡洛实验解决了不同的问题。首先，受控生成机制验证了在假设成立的情况下，所推导的规则能够恢复正确的概率。其次，相同的机制通过使用对数评分来衡量使用不匹配规则的后果。
tldr: 本文明确了不同概率合并规则（如平均、几率相乘）的适用条件，并通过蒙特卡洛实验验证了匹配规则的正确性和不匹配规则的后果，强调了规则选择需依据情境和风险。
en_tdlr: This paper clarifies the conditions under which different probability combination rules (e.g., averaging, odds multiplication) are appropriate, and uses Monte Carlo experiments to verify the correctness of matched rules and the consequences of mismatched ones, emphasizing that rule choice depends on the situation and stakes.
